messages:
sam_infra: heads up — after yesterday's driver rollout (NVIDIA 541.22 / CUDA 13.2) we've seen NVLink enumeration timeouts popping up on mixed H100/A100 racks in us-west-2. Several training batches fell back to SOCKET and throughput dropped ~3-4x.
ben_gpu_ops: any cluster-wide pattern? specific SKUs / instance types?
eva_sre: saw a couple alerts for high NCCL latency too. timestamps align with the driver daemon restart window around 02:10 UTC.
sam_infra: affected nodes are in pool-gpu-west-us (a mix of h100-80gb, a100-40gb). repro on one node: after reboot + driver, 
```
NCCL WARN Call to nvlinkEnumerate timed out for GPU 2
NCCL INFO P2P: SHM disabled, falling back to SOCKET
```
ben_gpu_ops: can you paste output of `nvidia-smi topo -m` and `cat /proc/driver/nvidia/version` from a repro host? also kernel version?
sam_infra: pasted minimal dump from host gpu-west-12: 
```
# /proc/driver/nvidia/version
NVRM version: NVIDIA UNIX x86_64 Kernel Module 541.22 Fri Feb 20 02:05:01 UTC 2026
# nvidia-smi topo -m
        GPU0    GPU1    GPU2
GPU0     X      NV1     SYS
GPU1    NV1      X      SYS
GPU2    SYS     SYS      X
```
ben_gpu_ops: that topology looks odd — NV1 only between 0/1, GPU2 is shown as SYS (no NVLink). on mixed nodes we usually expect NVLink between specific pairs. could be an enumeration race. please run `dmesg | grep -i nvlink` and `journalctl -k --no-pager | grep -i nvlink` and drop the results.
lisa_ml: also check `lsmod | grep nvidia` and whether the `nvidia-uvm` module is loaded before probe. we've seen ordering issues where uvmm/kern modules load late and probe misses links.
eva_sre: quick mitigation idea — for critical pools, mark driver rollout paused and roll back those nodes to 537.91 which had no incidents in canaries. can we automate a fast rollback?
sam_infra: deploy-bot shows the rollout window: `deploy-bot: rollout/driver-541.22 started for pool-gpu-west-us at 2026-02-20T02:08:13Z` — I can kick a rollback for the reserved dedicated racks.
ben_gpu_ops: before rollback, try forcing a re-probe sequence on an affected host: 
```
sudo rmmod nvidia_uvm nvidia_drm nvidia_modeset nvidia && sudo modprobe nvidia && sudo modprobe nvidia_uvm
# then check nvlink enumerations
nvidia-smi topo -m
```
If that restores NVLink links, it's an ordering/probe race. if not, we should capture `nvlibprobe` logs and file a ticket with driver vendor.
sam_infra: ran repro steps on gpu-west-12 — rmmod/modprobe restored NVLink between 0/1/2 but one node still shows SYS for GPU2 until a full kernel reboot. attaching dmesg snippet: 
```
[    3.412345] nvidia: nvlink: probe timeout waiting for link training on GPU2
[    3.412678] nvidia: nvlink: link training failed, disabling link
```
eva_sre: that matches an enumeration timeout. I agree rollback for dedicated and canary freeze for the rest. open action items: 1) rollback driver on reserved pools, 2) create alert that watches for sudden jump in NCCL socket fallback rate, 3) vendor bug report with logs and repro hosts.
ben_gpu_ops: adding a short-term NCCL env tweak? `NCCL_P2P_DISABLE=0 NCCL_SHM_DISABLE=0 NCCL_SOCKET_IFNAME=eth0` — not ideal but might reduce impact. also consider a daemon init ordering change: ensure nvidia modules load before container runtimes start (systemd unit tweak).
sam_infra: creating a rollback runbook and will kick off revert for 8 reserved racks now. I'll also tag infra-oncall to monitor. action: sam -> rollback, ben -> collect full nvlink probe logs and open vendor issue, eva -> block rollout and create alert, lisa -> patch init ordering PR.
lisa_ml: quick note — add a canary with mixed SKUs and force multiple reboots during canary to catch these ordering races early.
sam_infra: thanks all. I'll post an update when rollback completes. :eyes:
